class.name: ResolvedJoin
class.brief_description: One accepted player's join, with every field guaranteed present.
class.description: A session admits a peer by producing one of these, so code downstream of admission reads these fields rather than null-checking them. [method JoinPayload.resolve] builds it from what a peer asked for, the session's join gate accepts or replaces it, and [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_accepted_join] answers it for the rest of the peer's life. It is also a frame. The server sends the accepted join to every peer, so [method deserialize] reads bytes a remote peer wrote and refuses anything that does not spell a join rather than admitting a half-read one. [codeblock] # The session answers the join it accepted for a peer. var join := api.peer_get_accepted_join(peer_id) print(join.username, " joined as ", join.peer_id) [/codeblock]

method.name: deserialize
method.description: Reads a join from [param bytes], or [code]null[/code] when they do not spell one. [param bytes] arrive from a remote peer, so this refuses rather than trusting: bytes that are not a record, a record naming no [member peer_id] or [member username], and a [member peer_id] that is not a number all answer [code]null[/code]. [member arg_values] and [member is_debug] are optional and take their defaults, so a peer running an older build still sends a readable join.

method.name: serialize
method.description: Writes this join as the frame the server sends to every peer, which [method deserialize] reads back.

members.member: Typed join args the session's registered handler receives after this join, empty when the peer named no join intent. See [member JoinPayload.arg_values].
Whether this connection used debug initialization data.
The server peer id assigned to this player.
The player's display name. A session's join gate is what decides two peers may not hold one name, so this is unique only where that gate says it is.
